rappel_detail.anchor: a single old bolt or pin; back it up with a cam or nut
rappel_detail.station: A fixed station just below the summit block.
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel past the 5.3-5.6 friction-slab crux to a ledge.
hazards: The anchor does not inspire full confidence; back it up if in any doubt.

rappel_detail.anchor: a sling around a large wedged chockstone, sometimes with a rap ring
rappel_detail.station: The ledge below the slab crux.
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel through a band of loose rock and boulders to a notch, then downclimb and plunge-step the loose gully back onto the ascent talus.
rappel_detail.pull: A single 60 m rope used doubled is generally enough, but at least one party found it only just reached; knot the ends.
hazards: The gully channels rock kicked down by parties above; keep helmets on.

set.rappels: 2 rappels on a single 60 m rope, the first from a fixed station below the summit and the second from a slung chockstone; some parties break the descent into three shorter rappels
set.rappel_count_note: Most parties make two rappels with a single 60 m rope. Treat 60 m as the minimum, since one party found it only just reached. Depending on the exact gully line and rope length, some parties make three shorter rappels instead, and some report reaching the ledge in one long rappel from the summit. Lengths are not published.
